Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using hybrid search (semantic + keyword),
powered by the Entire search service.

Requires authentication via 'entire login' (GitHub device flow).

By default, results are scoped to the current repository. Use --all-repos to
search across all accessible repos.

Run without arguments to open an interactive search. Results are
displayed in an interactive table. Use --json for machine-readable output,
and add --compact for a trimmed per-result shape suited to agents (implies
--json): id, type, repo, branch, author, date, files touched, score, match
snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (repo hits add
description and checkpoint count). Fetch full detail
for a single result with 'entire checkpoint explain <id>', or add --full to
that command to pull the checkpoint's entire session transcript. For a
checkpoint hit from another GitHub repo, add --repo <owner/name> to
'entire checkpoint explain' (requires the full checkpoint ID; unrelated to
this command's --repo filter below).

CLI queries also support inline filters like author:<name>, date:<week|month>,
branch:<name>, repo:<owner/name>, and repo:* to search all accessible repos.

Usage:
  entire search [query] [flags]

Examples:
  entire search "retry backoff" --json
  entire search "retry backoff" --json --compact
  entire search "auth timeout author:alice date:week"
  entire search --code "parseToken"

Flags:
      --all-repos        Search all accessible repos instead of just the current one
      --author string    Filter by author name
      --branch string    Filter by branch name
      --case-sensitive   Case-sensitive code search (only with --code)
      --code             Search code content across repositories
      --compact          Trimmed JSON output for agents: id, repo, files touched, score, match snippet, and a truncated title instead of the full prompt (implies --json)
      --date string      Filter by time period (week or month)
  -h, --help             help for search
      --json             Output as JSON
      --limit int        Maximum number of results (per page for checkpoint search, total for --code) (default 10)
      --page int         Page number (1-based) (default 1)
      --repo strings     Filter by repository (gh/owner/repo, et/proj/repo, owner/repo, ULID, or *); repeatable and comma-separated for multiple repos

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)
=== CHECKPOINT ===
Operations on checkpoints — the persistent records of agent work tied to commits.

Commands:
  list     List checkpoints on the current branch
  explain  Explain a checkpoint, commit, or session
  tokens   Show token usage and optimization recommendations
  search   Search checkpoints (semantic + keyword)

Examples:
  entire checkpoint list
  entire checkpoint explain <id|sha>
  entire checkpoint tokens <id>
  entire checkpoint search "fix login"

Usage:
  entire checkpoint [command]

Aliases:
  checkpoint, cp, checkpoints

Available Commands:
  explain     Explain a session, commit, or checkpoint
  list        List checkpoints on the current branch
  search      Search checkpoints, commits, and sessions using semantic and keyword matching
  tokens      Show token usage and optimization recommendations for a checkpoint

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for checkpoint

Global Flags:
      --context name   Act as this saved login name for this command only, instead of the active context (entire auth contexts lists them)

Use "entire checkpoint [command] --help" for more information about a command.
=== EXPLAIN ===
Explain provides human-readable context about sessions, commits, and checkpoints.

Use this command to understand what happened during agent-driven development,
either for self-review or to understand a teammate's work.

By default, shows checkpoints on the current branch. Pass a checkpoint ID or
commit SHA as a positional argument to explain a specific item, or use flags.

Viewing specific items:
  entire checkpoint explain <id-or-sha>           Auto-detects checkpoint ID or commit SHA
  entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id>     Force interpretation as checkpoint ID
  entire checkpoint explain --commit <ref>        Force interpretation as commit ref

Checkpoints in another repo:
  entire checkpoint explain <id> --repo owner/name
                 Explain a checkpoint owned by another repository — the
                 drill-down for a cross-repo 'entire search' hit. Reads it from
                 that repo's Entire API; nothing is written to this repo.
                 Needs a full checkpoint ID (positional or --checkpoint) and a
                 checkpoint that has been pushed.

Filtering the list view:
  --session      Filter checkpoints by session ID (or prefix)

Output verbosity levels (when explaining a specific item):
  Default:         Detailed view with scoped prompts (ID, session, tokens, intent, prompts, files)
  --short          Summary only (ID, session, timestamp, tokens, intent)
  --full           Parsed full transcript (all prompts/responses from entire session)
  --raw-transcript Raw transcript file (JSONL format)

Machine-readable export modes (additive surface for external consumers):
  --json           Metadata-only JSON. Lists checkpoints when no target is given;
                   emits a single checkpoint envelope when a target is supplied.
                   Transcript bytes are NEVER embedded in the JSON envelope.
  --transcript     Stream stored checkpoint transcript bytes (JSONL) to stdout
                   for the selected session. Same bytes as --raw-transcript
                   while checkpoints v1 is the checkpoint store.
  --session-index  Pick a session within a multi-session checkpoint (0-based).
                   Defaults to the latest session. Only meaningful with
                   --transcript or --raw-transcript.
  --limit          Cap the number of checkpoints returned by the list view.
                   Defaults to 100. When the cap is hit, a stderr note
                   says how many were skipped. Only meaningful with --json.

Summary generation:
  --generate    Generate an AI summary for the checkpoint
  --force       Regenerate even if a summary already exists (requires --generate)

Performance options:
  --search-all  Remove branch/depth limits when searching for commits (may be slow)

Checkpoint detail view shows:
  - Author of the checkpoint
  - Associated git commits that reference the checkpoint
  - Prompts and responses from the session

Note: --session filters the list view; the positional arg, --commit, and --checkpoint are mutually exclusive.

Usage:
  entire checkpoint explain [checkpoint-id | commit-sha] [flags]

## Run the demo from `tedlasso-strava/`, not the 2.0 parent

This is the thing that would bite you on stage. From the parent repo, `entire search` returns great hits, but every drill-down fails:

```

no checkpoint or commit found matching "07d55332..."
```

The hits belong to `elizabethsiegle/tedlasso-strava`, the nested repo. `cd tedlasso-strava` first and the exact same command resolves. Also note only the two checkpoints on `feat/route-basemap` resolve locally; main-branch commits like `4515e5cf` hit `checkpoint not found: 01M04D4F1FDB...` because that checkpoint hasn't been fetched. Stay on the current branch's checkpoints.

## Tier 1: the search-to-explain money shot

These score 40+ and return a **session hit paired with its commit**, and `explain` resolves cleanly:

```bash
entire search "overlay the route on a city street map"      # session 51.5 + commit 69121be
entire search "timezone handling for late night runs"       # session 42.1 + commit 07d5533
entire search "proxy map tiles through the worker"          # 36.9
```

Then drill in. The commit sha straight from the search result works as the argument:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain 69121be
```

That prints the intent (`"could you make the map also include the map of the city?"`), all 15 touched files, and the full transcript with every tool call the agent made. That is the part people have not seen before.

## Tier 2: proving it isn't grep

Queries with near-zero literal overlap that still land on the right session. Worth doing one of these right after a Tier 1, because it kills the "so it's just search" objection:

```bash
entire search "why does the run say yesterday"              # 18.8, nails the tz fix
entire search "making the UI not look AI generated"         # 15.1, hits the superpowers build session
entire search "what did the agent do when the API returned garbage"   # sessions only, 13.5
```

`"why does the run say yesterday"` is my pick for the single best line in the demo. It is how a human actually reports a bug, nobody wrote those words anywhere, and it returns exactly one session and one commit. No noise to explain away.

## On your `"cold path failover tests"` example

It works, but it is the weakest of the bunch for this demo: one commit hit, no session. Same for `"KV outage failover"` (2 commits) and `"rate limit 429 backoff"` (zero hits, avoid that one). Your infra-flavored phrasing pulls commits; the map and timezone work is where the *sessions* are indexed.

Also worth a mention if you have time: bare `entire search` opens an interactive table, `--compact` is the agent-facing shape, and inline filters (`author:lizzie`, `date:week`, `repo:*`) work in the query string itself.

Diagnosed both halves. Here's what's actually going on.

## Checkpoints *are* being searched, they're just not labeled as such

Nothing is missing from the index. I searched the text of checkpoint `01M0G0WDKY...`'s own intent (`"could you make the map also include the map of the city"`), which appears nowhere in the commit message `feat: draw the route over a proxied street basemap`:

```
counts: {'checkpoints': 1, 'sessions': 1, 'commits': 0}
  commit   17.91  69121be7ddf40ad...  feat: draw the route over a proxied stre
  session  17.91  6d3b3863-c889-4b...  commit
```

`counts.checkpoints: 1` means a checkpoint matched. The identical 17.91 on both rows means that is one record surfaced twice, as its commit and its session. Across a 30-result sweep, zero result ids were checkpoint ULIDs. So a checkpoint tied to a commit always renders as the commit row, and you reach it with `explain`. That's a labeling gap in the results table, not absent data.

## But this repo's checkpoints genuinely aren't indexed

This is the bigger problem:

| | parent `tedlasso-strava2.0` | nested `tedlasso-strava/` |
|---|---|---|
| local checkpoint refs | **5** | 2 |
| on origin | **0** | 2 |
| upstream for `main` | none configured | tracked, in sync |
| shared history with origin | **none** | yes |

Both point at the same remote (`gh/elizabethsiegle/tedlasso-strava`), but the parent shares no commits with it and `main` has no upstream, so its 5 checkpoints have never shipped. That includes the good one, `01M0B7KR4RZQD8A8SMVH9VBET3` "Add implementation plan for Ted Lasso Strava mood board", plus a large `[temporary]` one spanning ~45 commits. Every hit in my earlier searches came from the nested repo. Pushing parent `main` there would be an unrelated-histories push, so I did not.

## The good news for making one right now

Your current session is registered in **both** worktrees, and in the nested repo it reads:

```
Worktree: tedlasso-strava   Status: active   Checkpoints: 0
Last prompt: "amazing now i really need a checkpoint..."
```

The nested repo is correctly wired and its checkpoints demonstrably push and index. It also has four uncommitted tooling files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.entire/settings.json`, `.entire/.gitignore`), and that repo already has precedent for exactly this commit (`1f0f1a72 chore: enable Entire tracking`). So a commit there produces a real checkpoint attached to this session, and a push makes it searchable.

That last step touches your remote, so I want your call before I do it.
